steps.explain: Find the third angle inside the left right-angled triangle
steps.work:
In the left right-angled triangle, the sum of interior angles is \(180^\circ\):

\[90^\circ + 45^\circ + \theta = 180^\circ\]

\[\theta = 180^\circ - 135^\circ = 45^\circ\]

So the interior angle at the intersection point is \(45^\circ\).

steps.explain: Use the straight-line angle property to find angle Y
steps.work:
The horizontal line is a straight line, which forms an angle of \(180^\circ\). Angle \(Y\) and the interior angle \(45^\circ\) form a supplementary linear pair:

\[Y + 45^\circ = 180^\circ\]

\[Y = 180^\circ - 45^\circ = \mathbf{135^\circ}\]

(Note: The \(60^\circ\) angle in the right triangle is extra information and is not required to solve for \(Y\).)

steps.explain: Find the combined value of ● and △ using Row 3
steps.work:
Look at Row 3, which consists only of ● and △:

\[2 \times ● + 2 \times △ = 20 \implies ● + △ = 10\]

steps.explain: Find the values of □, ●, and △ using Column 1 and Row 2
steps.work:
In Column 1: \[2 \times ● + △ + □ = 22\]

Since \(● + △ = 10\), we have \(● + □ + 10 = 22 \implies ● + □ = 12\), so \(● = 12 - □\).

In Row 2: \[3 \times □ + ● = 28\]

Substitute \(● = 12 - □\):

\[3 \times □ + (12 - □) = 28 \implies 2 \times □ + 12 = 28 \implies 2 \times □ = 16 \implies \mathbf{□ = 8}\]

Then find ● and △:

\[● = 12 - 8 = \mathbf{4}\]

\[△ = 10 - 4 = \mathbf{6}\]

steps.explain: Calculate the value of ★ using Row 1
steps.work:
Substitute the known values \(● = 4\) and \(△ = 6\) into Row 1:

\[● + △ + ★ + △ = 25\]

\[4 + 6 + ★ + 6 = 25\]

\[16 + ★ = 25 \implies ★ = 25 - 16 = \mathbf{9}\]

(Check with Column 3: \(9 + 2(8) + 6 = 9 + 16 + 6 = 31\), which matches.)

steps.explain: Analyze painted faces of a single-layer cube structure
steps.work:
The 3D shape is 1 cube deep (consisting of \(13\) unit cubes in total). Because the entire outside is painted:

  • Every cube has its front face painted.
  • Every cube has its back face painted.

Therefore, every cube already has at least \(2\) painted faces.

steps.explain: Identify the condition for exactly three painted faces
steps.work:
For a cube to have only 3 painted faces, it must have exactly 1 additional face exposed (from top, bottom, left, or right).

This means the cube must touch other cubes on 3 of its 4 side edges, leaving exactly one outer edge exposed.

steps.explain: Count the qualifying cubes row by row
steps.work:
Checking each row:

  • Top row (4 cubes): The 2nd and 3rd cubes from the left are surrounded on the left, right, and bottom (only their top face is exposed) \( ightarrow\) 2 cubes.
  • Middle row (6 cubes): The 1st cube on the left is surrounded on top, right, and bottom (only left exposed). The 4th cube from the left is surrounded on top, left, and right (only bottom exposed) \( ightarrow\) 2 cubes.
  • Bottom row (3 cubes): The 2nd cube from the left is surrounded on the left, top, and right (only bottom exposed) \( ightarrow\) 1 cube.

\[ ext{Total} = 2 + 2 + 1 = \mathbf{5 ext{ cubes}}\]

parts.stem: How many Year 6 students were surveyed altogether?

steps.explain: Calculate the combined percentage for Popcorn and Chocolate
steps.work:
First convert the angle for Popcorn to a percentage:

\[ ext{Popcorn} = rac{36^\circ}{360^\circ} imes 100\% = 10\%\]

Chocolate is given as \(28\%\). Combined:

\[ ext{Popcorn} + ext{Chocolate} = 10\% + 28\% = 38\%\]

steps.explain: Find the percentage represented by the remaining snack categories
steps.work:
The remaining categories are Soft Drink, Chips, and Lollies:

\[ ext{Percentage} = 100\% - 38\% = 62\%\]

steps.explain: Sum the known student counts and calculate total students
steps.work:
Sum the student numbers for Soft Drink, Chips, and Lollies:

\[10 + 40 + 74 = 124 ext{ students}\]

Since \(124 ext{ students}\) represents \(62\%\) of the total:

\[1\% = rac{124}{62} = 2 ext{ students}\]

\[ ext{Total students (100\%)} = 2 imes 100 = \mathbf{200 ext{ students}}\]

questions.stem: Vivian has a 60 L bath which is filled to the brim. As the plug is stuck, she has to use a pump to pump out all the water. If the pump pumps water out at a rate of 1.5 L per minute, how long will it take for the pump to have pumped out 75% of the bath water?

steps.explain: Explanation
steps.work:
\(60L \times 75\% = 45L\)

\(45/1.5 = 30\) minutes

questions.stem: Riya did some vocabulary tests. Excluding the mark of her last exam, her average mark was 18. In her last test, she achieved a mark of 13, which brought her average down to 17. How many tests did Riya sit altogether?

steps.explain: Explanation
steps.work:
Let x be number of tests done.

Total after last test = \(17 \times x\)

Total before last test = \((x-1) \times 18\)

Total after last test = \((x-1) \times 18 + 13\)

\((x-1) \times 18 + 13 = 17 \times x\)

\(18x - 5 = 17x\)

\(x = 5\)

questions.stem: A certain garden has a path built around it. How long is the path? (Note: they are both parallelograms)

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 380 185" style="max-width: 380px; width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; margin: 0 auto;"><g stroke="#1e293b" stroke-width="1.8" fill="none" stroke-linejoin="round"><polygon points="40,140 210,140 230,50 60,50"/><polygon points="210,140 310,140 324.3,75.7 224.3,75.7"/></g><g font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="13.5" font-weight="600" fill="#0f172a"><text x="125" y="162" text-anchor="middle">17 cm</text><text x="260" y="162" text-anchor="middle">10 cm</text><text x="198" y="98" text-anchor="end">7 cm</text><text x="332" y="112" text-anchor="start">5 cm</text></g></svg>

steps.explain: Calculate the total length of the horizontal edges
steps.work:
Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal:

  • Bottom path: \(17\text{ cm} + 10\text{ cm} = 27\text{ cm}\)
  • Top path: \(17\text{ cm} + 10\text{ cm} = 27\text{ cm}\)

\[\text{Horizontal Length} = 27\text{ cm} + 27\text{ cm} = 54\text{ cm}\]

steps.explain: Calculate the total length of the slanted outer edges
steps.work:
For the slanted sides:

  • Left outer slanted side: \(7\text{ cm}\)
  • Right outer slanted side: \(5\text{ cm}\)
  • Step where the large parallelogram extends above the small one: \(7\text{ cm} - 5\text{ cm} = 2\text{ cm}\)

\[\text{Slanted Length} = 7\text{ cm} + 5\text{ cm} + 2\text{ cm} = 14\text{ cm}\]

steps.explain: Sum all outer edges to find the total perimeter of the path
steps.work:
Add the horizontal and slanted components together:

\[\text{Total Path Length} = 54\text{ cm} + 14\text{ cm} = \mathbf{68\text{ cm}}\]

(Equivalent formula: \(2 \times (17 + 10) + 2 \times 7 = 54 + 14 = 68\text{ cm}\))

questions.stem: A reservoir is \(\frac{3}{7}\) full. If 120 litres of water is added, the reservoir is \(\frac{9}{11}\) full. What is the capacity (in litres) of the reservoir when full?

steps.explain: Explanation
steps.work:
\(\frac{9}{11} - \frac{3}{7} = \frac{30}{77}\)

This is equal to 120 L, therefore 1/77 of the total capacity = 4 L

Total capacity = \(4 \times 77 = 308\)L

questions.stem:
Questions 34 and 35 use the following information.

In a lawn bowls club, there are 280 members, five sevenths of whom are men. All of the members participate in either bowling or scoring. Two fifths of the women and one half of men do bowling.

parts.stem: How many men do scoring?

steps.explain: Explanation
steps.work:
\(280 \times 5/7 = 200\) men

half of men score – 100 men scoring

parts.stem: What fraction of all the members do scoring?

steps.explain: Explanation
steps.work:
100 men scoring

80 women in total, scoring = \(3/5 \times 80 = 48\)

Total scorers = 148

Fraction = \(148/280 = 37/70\)
